message.content: {"decision":"accept","reason":"This GitHub blog post provides detailed data over nine quarters showing that the rise in secret leaks is due to increased push volume rather than developer carelessness, with evidence from push prevalence rates and override statistics. It also introduces a new fine-tuned classifier that improves secret detection speed and coverage, and explains how push protection blocks secrets before they enter repository history, reducing human remediation effort. This directly affects what learners can delegate to AI agents and highlights the importance of platform-level prevention to keep pace with accelerated code creation, making it highly relevant for learners managing secrets in their code.","piece_ids":["01"],"strongest_claim":"The increase in leaked secrets in public code is due to accelerated code creation outpacing human remediation, not developer carelessness, and new AI-driven push protection can prevent many secrets from entering repository history, reducing manual cleanup.","evidence_type":"data","perspective":"vendor","commercial_incentive":true}
